title: How McDonald's Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with Devo's lawsuit against McDonald's over the New Wave Nigel Happy Meal toy's flowerpot hat, then trace McDonald's history: the McDonald brothers' San Bernardino hot dog and barbecue stands, the Speedy System assembly-line approach, Ray Kroc as multimixer salesman turned franchising agent, the Harry Sonneborn real estate model, the buyout, the public offering and Dow inclusion, and Ronald McDonald and early characters (with the Sid and Marty Krofft lawsuit). They cover site selection, drive-through call centers, cleanliness and global expansion, menu item origins (Filet-O-Fish, Big Mac, Egg McMuffin, Chicken McNugget), criticism (McLibel case, hot coffee lawsuit, beef fat fries, Fast Food Nation, Super Size Me), Ronald McDonald House charities, glocalization, and famous former employees. Listener mail is teased but not read; a New York City happy hour and t-shirt contest are announced.
topics: stuff you should know listener mail

segments.title: Devo lawsuit and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with Devo music and discuss Devo's lawsuit against McDonald's over the New Wave Nigel Happy Meal toy's hat, which resembles Devo's trademarked energy dome hats.

segments.title: McDonald brothers and early history
segments.summary: The McDonald brothers, Dick and Mac, ran a movie theater, then opened a hot dog stand in Arcadia, later moved to San Bernardino and became a barbecue-style burger, fries and shake restaurant before retooling.

segments.title: Speedy System and assembly line fast food
segments.summary: The brothers created the Speedy System, applying assembly line principles to food preparation, eliminating car hops and reshaping fast food.

segments.title: Ray Kroc becomes franchising agent
segments.summary: Ray Kroc, a multimixer salesman, noticed the brothers ordering eight multimixers, visited San Bernardino, and became their franchising agent. He opened the first franchise in Des Plaines, Illinois.

segments.title: Real estate model and buyout
segments.summary: Harry Sonneborn devised a real estate model where the company leased land and subleased it to franchisees with markups, making the real estate arm as profitable as the restaurants. Kroc bought out the brothers in 1961 for 2.7 million dollars, and the brothers reopened a competing restaurant, the Big M.

segments.title: Going public, Dow inclusion and Ronald McDonald
segments.summary: McDonald's went public in 1965, later joined the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and targeted kids with characters starting with Ronald McDonald, introduced by Willard Scott.

segments.title: McDonaldland characters and Sid and Marty Krofft lawsuit
segments.summary: McDonald's added characters such as Hamburglar, Grimace and Mayor McCheese. Their look was alleged to copy Sid and Marty Krofft shows, and the Kroffts were awarded fifty thousand dollars. Grimace was originally designed as an evil three-armed character.

segments.title: Site selection and drive-through call centers
segments.summary: Hosts describe how McDonald's picks locations near intersections, schools and airports, the physical building requirements, automation such as fry cookers, and drive-through orders taken by call centers in other states with photos of customers.

segments.title: Cleanliness, global expansion and menu history
segments.summary: Ray Kroc's focus on cleanliness and McDonald's influence on Hong Kong bathroom standards and queuing. The hosts then discuss origins of the Filet-O-Fish, Hula Burger, Big Mac, Egg McMuffin, and Chicken McNugget.

segments.title: Wrap-up and listener mail call
segments.summary: The hosts announce a New York City happy hour and a t-shirt design contest, then sign off.
topics: stuff you should know listener mail
